evals.prompt: Explain the atomic transaction protocol for editing a Canva design, including how to handle responsive pages and what happens if the user rejects a preview.
asserts: Enforces start-editing-transaction -> perform-editing-operations -> commit-editing-transaction sequence
Specifies that cancel-editing-transaction must be called to safely discard drafts upon rejection
Identifies restricted operations on responsive pages where is_responsive is true
Enforces explicit user visual approval before executing commit

evals.prompt: How does the brand checker handle the data gap when Canva:list-brand-kits returns only names and thumbnails without machine-readable hex colors or fonts?
asserts: Identifies that brand kits often omit machine-readable hex codes and font families
Falls back to visual comparison of thumbnails and prompts user for explicit brand values
Uses the three-state verdict: On brand, Off brand, and Can't verify
Distinguishes API-fixable properties from manual editor constraints

evals.prompt: Describe the three patterns for handling image fields during CSV bulk creation with Canva Brand Templates.
asserts: Specifies Pattern A for pre-existing Canva asset IDs
Specifies Pattern B for remote image URLs requiring upload-asset-from-url pre-flight
Specifies Pattern C for missing image columns where placeholder is skipped or retained
Emphasizes sequential row-by-row execution rather than concurrent unthrottled calls

evals.prompt: When a user asks to resize a Canva presentation for all social media channels without specifying dimensions, how should dimensions be resolved?
asserts: Applies the default channel set: 1080x1920 (Stories/Reels/TikTok/Shorts), 1080x1350 (Feed portrait), 1200x627 (LinkedIn/X/FB link), 1920x1080 (YouTube)
Deduplicates near-identical landscape canvases (1200x627, 1200x628, 1200x630) into 1200x627
Executes resize-design for each unique canvas and returns direct Canva edit links
Does not prompt for placement clarification when all channels are generically requested

evals.prompt: How should an AI agent triage 15 reviewer comments on a Canva deck, and when should the user be prompted for approval?
asserts: Categorizes feedback into Actionable, Requires Manual Action, and Resolved
Classifies font family and new text box requests under Requires Manual Action
Prompts the user for approval exactly ONE time on the unified plan
Automatically commits approved edits and replies to comment threads without secondary approval prompts
